text: Not quite, Mayor, since I know I took up a lot of your time at the last meeting. Just a few items to report. The first is I'm pleased to announce that once again, the city has been identified as a well city by Association of Washington Cities. I'd like to extend a hearty congratulations to our Human Resources Director, Mary McDougal, her team, and of course, our Wellness Committee for their leadership. And once again, focusing on employee wellness and safety. On the legislative front, wanted to point out that the house earlier this weekend released its operating budget, and included in there is $250,000 that the city had requested for a study to identify current facilities where state hospitals, specifically Western State and Eastern State Hospital, are releasing folks to. This request by the City of Lakewood really focuses on two items. One is to demonstrate that the current facilities where folks are being released into, particularly from Western State Hospital, are disproportionately located, not just in Pierce County, but Lakewood as well. And then secondly, demonstrate the state's needs to invest in other facilities so that as individuals are released from, for example, Western State Hospital, they are going to the appropriate facility for their care to be able to continue. And I wanna thank our state legislators from the 28th District for helping with that. This now moves over to the Senate side for their review and consideration. And so we'll continue to track this and keep you posted of what's going on there. Also, I just wanted to let you know, I'm gonna be meeting, actually myself and my team, we're gonna be meeting with the Pierce Transit CEO and his team here in the next few weeks to talk about Bus Rapid Transit 2 and coming into Lakewood. And as you know, the policy direction from this body is that the next round of Bus Rapid Transit, as it comes out of Tacoma, specifically the Tacoma Dome and onto South Tacoma Way and South into Lakewood, South Tacoma Way and Lakewood, and then it will cross Pacific Highway and come up on Pacific Highway. Our goal is for it to continue all the way down Pacific Highway to be able to connect into Springbrook and then further down into Tillicum to be able to connect there. And of course, have access to JBLM. That is something that we have not been able to get much traction on. Right now, Pierce Transit is proposing that once Bus Rapid Transit, or this is our understanding, that's the point of the meeting is to get some clarity on this, is for it to then cut, as it crosses over 512 onto Pacific Highway, then it'll hang a hard right on 108 and then end up in the Lakewood Transit Center, which is fine. And then from there, get onto Bridgeport and head into University Place, which again is great, but our concern is we would like BRT to continue further south on Pacific Highway so that it gets into areas where folks in need of transportation alternatives have access to that.
